html:
SMTO-SCH-0020 — SMTO couldn't pin down the exact time for this schedule

GUID: a26a207e-0655-4563-99c3-d64ea0c59cda
Slug: schedule-anchor-invalid
Domain: SCH · Subsystem: sch

What happened

  • When you ask for something at a set time, SMTO links the schedule to your original message and an exact time zone. That link was missing here, so no schedule was created.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Schedules and use Search schedules to look for the work you asked for. This tells you for sure whether anything was scheduled before you set it up again.
  2. If it isn't there, select New schedule, enter the instruction, pick the date, time and Time zone, then select Create schedule. The schedule editor always saves an exact time with its time zone.
  3. Or ask the Agent again in a new message with the full time and zone, for example "tomorrow at 9:00 PM Eastern time". A new message gives SMTO a fresh request to link the schedule to.

What success looks like

  • One schedule for your request appears on the Schedules page with the right Next run time.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't create several copies while checking; look on the Schedules page first.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Schedule creation rejected an anchored due_at that has no timezone offset or no temporal_request_id linking it to the original request.

What this means

  • Anchored due_at parsing finds no timezone offset or no temporal_request_id tying it to its original request. Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.

Why this can happen

  • Anchored due_at parsing finds no timezone offset or no temporal_request_id tying it to its original request.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the aware timestamp and captured temporal identity from the supported scheduling flow.

How to fix it

  • _create_event_locked (and MemoryEventStore.create_event) require an anchored due_at to be timezone-aware and to carry the temporal_request_id from temporal routing. This normally means the caller passed due_at outside the supported scheduling flow; create the schedule through temporal routing or the Schedules API without due_at, using next_run_at plus timezone.
  • Supply a time with an explicit UTC offset and the original request identity through the supported scheduling flow.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • One exact original temporal request owns the timezone-aware trigger.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
